To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Data quality is an important issue for the smart city.
Data quality is important to the development and success of urban applications, and that the lack of data veracity and quality reporting can lead to poor smart cities and applications.
Data quality issues can propagate throughout a data ecosystem and lead to unreliable smart city applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to improve the quality of data in the absence of documentation by the data providers, and in particular how to improve the veracity of open urban data.
the veracity of urban data and how this can be assessed and improved.
the veracity of urban open data and how to assess it in the absence of metadata and user documentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are not fit for purpose.
data are only as good as the people who use them.
the quality of data provided through open government data portals is highly variable and that it is the responsibility of data consumers to ensure that the data they use is fit for purpose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of open government data portals is not as high as they should be and that the quality of the data is not being adequately reported.
we have shown how to improve the veracity of data by using crowdsourced knowledge and by documenting the data cleaning process in the form of a data lineage.

we have demonstrated that the quality of urban datasets can be significantly enhanced through a combination of data science and crowdsourcing techniques, and that this approach can be used to improve the veracity of urban data and the reliability of applications which use them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data quality is not just an issue to be considered in the development and deployment of smart city applications but is also an issue for the open government data movement.
data quality is a shared responsibility of the data provider, data users, and the data portal.
data veracity is not a given and needs to be actively maintained.
